newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to April 18.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to April 18.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Monday a 66.79 percent increase in its turnover last week on a slightly improved market liquidity.
Total turnover rose to 47.495 million dinars ($8.36 million) in 230 deals from 28.476 million dinars in 200 transactions in the previous week.
"Liquidity has slightly improved but we do not know where the money is coming from. And companies are taking advantage of improved market liquidity to enter fresh borrowing," a trader told Reuters.
For the week ending April 18, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 209 times for a volume of 33.615 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for five deals worth 0.472 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 520 percent while maturity stood at between seven and 30 days.
* National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) short-term bonds traded twice for a volume of eight million dinars.
* Certificates of deposit accounted for nine deals totalling 1.493 million dinars.
* The NBY continued to sell part of its bond portfolio on the secondary market. The central bank sold 3.915 million dinars worth of bonds issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper, treasury bills and certificates of deposit fell to 24.673 million dinars from 30.884 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 15.1 million dinars from 17.13 million a week ago.
